- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.4) after a recent dip, model tends to overestimate and overshoots; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >+10% from prior 3-day avg), model often overreacts and forecasts higher than true; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true values in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply 3–7% upward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is systematically underestimating; apply 5–10% upward adjustment for next 5 days.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., ±0.8 swings), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% forecast deviation from true for 3–5 day windows.
